assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, the incretin effect, glucagon-like peptide actions on islets, satiety and gastric emptying) translated into long-acting agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all high, and the arc from physiology to medicine fits the prize well.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across basic physiology (Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, and others not on this list) and drug development (Knudsen). Holst and Drucker are the strongest physiological anchors; Knudsen represents the pharmacological translation. Mojsov's contribution on the active peptide GLP-1(7-36) is real, and the three-person limit forces a hard choice that I cannot resolve from the supplied credit alone.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of replication, multiple approved drugs, large outcome trials and broad clinical uptake. Timely and arguably overdue given the scale of impact.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen is contested, and other early contributors may not appear in the credited names.
Whether the committee prefers recognition of the physiology or of the drug development is unresolved.
My knowledge of the detailed priority disputes is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality (living drugs). The concept, the costimulatory design and the clinical proof are each important, with strong and lasting impact on cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain made the decisive CAR design and first-in-human work, with Sadelain on second-generation CD28 CARs and June on 4-1BB CARs and the CD19 trials. Rosenberg contributed foundational adoptive cell therapy, TIL and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Eshhar and others not listed are also historically important, so the supplied credit may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the clinic, with multiple approved products, long-term remissions and independent confirmation. Ongoing questions about solid tumors, toxicity and access do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Early priority (Eshhar and others) may lie outside the credited names.
Whether Rosenberg's role is better seen as adjacent adoptive-cell-therapy work than CAR-T itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial opsins turned into tools for millisecond-precision, cell-type-specific control of neural activity. The methodological impact on neuroscience is enormous, and the originality is clear. Its medical impact is mostly in enabling research, with early clinical translation (vision restoration) only beginning.
assessment.attribution: Credit divides across the discovery and characterization of channelrhodopsin (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), the first neuronal demonstrations (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier conceptual work (Miesenböck). With six credited people and a three-laureate limit, this is a difficult configuration, and any choice leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely adopted for over a decade, so mature as a technology. Therapeutic validation remains limited.
uncertainties: Allocation is highly disputed among six names.
Physiology or Medicine relevance rests on the research tool rather than on a therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response is a conceptual advance showing how the ER communicates its folding state to the nucleus. It is clear, original and broadly explanatory across physiology and disease, including diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell function.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the signaling pathway (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing), and their joint contribution is well-defined and compact. Other work on PERK/ATF6 is also relevant but the core configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation and an extensive literature. Timely, as it is a classic Lasker-level fundamental discovery that has yet to be recognized.
uncertainties: Direct medical translation is still emerging, with the strongest case being fundamental cell biology.
Contributions of others (for example, Ron, Harding, Kaufman) could be argued to deserve inclusion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and as a central regulator of cell growth and metabolism created a major field. It has wide implications for cancer, diabetes, aging and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall's identification of TOR in yeast is the decisive discovery. Contributions from Schreiber on FKBP12-rapamycin and Sabatini on mTOR in mammals are important but secondary, and the credit is separable. A Hall-only or Hall-plus-one configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with extensive independent confirmation and drugs (rapalogs) in clinical use. Timely and widely recognized.
uncertainties: Whether to include a second laureate and, if so, who; Sabatini's inclusion could be sensitive for reasons unrelated to the science.
Earlier work on rapamycin's mechanism complicates the scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and successor BCR-ABL inhibitors established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and converted chronic myeloid leukemia from fatal to manageable. The importance and clarity are very high, and the biological rationale built on the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (chemistry and compound development), Druker (clinical proof and advocacy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. The upstream discovery of BCR-ABL and the Philadelphia chromosome (Rowley, Gallo-type work, others) falls outside the credited names, which weakens the framing for a pure drug-development award.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with long-term survival data and wide replication. Recognition would be timely, though it has been waiting for some years and the field's heroes may be seen as already honored by other prizes.
uncertainties: Excluded earlier discoverers (cytogenetics, BCR-ABL cloning) may be seen as rightful co-recipients.
Industry-versus-academic credit for Lydon is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VLP-based HPV vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level evidence of reduced disease. The impact on public health and the prevention of cancer is very large, and the VLP technology was an original conceptual step.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP work at NCI) and Frazer (together with Zhou, who died in 1999, on VLP formation) are the main figures. The posthumous role of Jian Zhou and the parallel work of other groups complicate a fair three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with long-term surveillance data showing reductions in HPV infection, precancer and now invasive cancer. Zur Hausen's 2008 prize on HPV and cervical cancer addresses an adjacent discovery, so some may see overlap, though the vaccine itself is distinct.
uncertainties: The late Jian Zhou's credit cannot be reflected in a laureate list.
Overlap with the earlier HPV recognition and parallel development at the pharmaceutical firms is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 exon 7 splicing, leading to nusinersen, is a case of mechanism-based RNA therapeutics changing the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy. It is original and clinically transformative, and it connects splicing biology to a therapy.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing regulatory elements and ASO design) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a compact configuration. Contributions from others in SMN2 splicing and SMA genetics (for example Lefebvre, Melki, Singh and Hua) may matter, and these are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with approval in 2016 and a consistent real-world and long-term trial record. It may be somewhat early relative to other candidates, and the broader antisense field's recognition could be viewed as a larger compound discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be for SMN2 splicing correction specifically or antisense therapeutics more generally.
Competing credit for SMN gene discovery (not on the credited list).
